assumption: deadline (SLA) jobs sold = 60% of the fleet's yearly heat-matched capacity, flat over the year; sensitivity sweep 0.3-1.2 in results
Best-effort spot work without deadline (e.g. public-archive embedding, evaluation sweeps, rendering) fills any remaining heat budget. Always available on GPU spot markets.
assumption: spot/backfill sells at ~50% of on-demand (typical cloud spot discount 50-70%)
assumption: batch SLAs 'next business day'
ElCom 2026 H4 total price per BFS municipality, fetched live by scripts/fetch_data.py -> data/derived/elcom_sites_2026.json (Basel 33.25 ... Zermatt 22.32 Rp/kWh)

dispatcher tie-break towards cheaper electricity. Tested at 0.05: no fleet cost effect, because backfill fills every heat budget anyway, so each site's electricity use is set by its heat demand. Regional prices therefore matter for per-site economics (see map), not for routing.
assumption: residential internet / server faults (two events per site per year)
assumption: until a technician / ISP restores service

Open-Meteo forecast horizon used in practice is 7 days; we plan 36 h ahead
assumption: typical day-ahead 2 m temperature RMSE at 24 h lead (MeteoSwiss verification order of magnitude)
tuned on 2025 (sweep 0.7/0.8/0.9): planning on 70% of forecast heat sink gives fewest rejections AND misses (less over-commitment cascade)
tuned together with forecast_trust
